_comment: Source manifest for every planetary texture. 'fidelity' is one of: scientific-map (spacecraft data mosaic), derived (processed from scientific data), artistic-composite (NOT a scientific map), procedural (generated by Atlas, no imagery). Nothing here is presented as more than its fidelity.

textures.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit (SVS 4720)
textures.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio; Ernie Wright (STC); Noah Petro (NASA/GSFC); LRO LROC and LOLA instrument teams
textures.license: NASA media: not copyrighted; credit requested (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)
textures.projection: equirectangular (simple cylindrical), global, centred on 0 deg longitude
textures.processing: none beyond resampling to 2048x1024 and 512x256 (Lanczos). Colour map adapted by SVS from the LROC WAC Hapke-normalised mosaic (over 100,000 WAC images); the 2019/2025 SVS maps are processed for 3D rendering.

textures.source: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute, Cassini Best Maps of Jupiter Cylindrical Map (PIA07782)
textures.license: NASA media: not copyrighted; credit requested
textures.projection: simple cylindrical, global, built from Cassini narrow-angle camera images during the Dec 2000 flyby
textures.lon_note: Longitude origin and direction of this map were NOT verified (the official caption could not be read). Standard cartographic orientation (east to the right, north up) is assumed; Jupiter has no fixed surface, so the only consequence is the position of the Great Red Spot in longitude.

textures.source: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio, Equirectangular Projected Earth (SVS 3615); Blue Marble Next Generation data courtesy of Reto Stockli (NASA/GSFC) and NASA's Earth Observatory
textures.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio; Blue Marble Next Generation data courtesy of Reto Stockli (NASA/GSFC) and NASA's Earth Observatory
textures.license: NASA media: not copyrighted; credit requested
textures.projection: equirectangular, global, centred on 0 deg longitude
textures.note: SVS states the look (cloud appearance, ocean colouring) was ART-DIRECTED for a film. Derived from Blue Marble Next Generation but not a pure scientific product.

textures.source: NASA/GSFC SVS 3615 (difference of the with-clouds and no-clouds renders of the same scene)
textures.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
textures.license: NASA media: not copyrighted; credit requested
textures.processing: cloud opacity = clamp(luminance(with clouds) - luminance(no clouds), 0..1) rescaled; this is an extraction from an art-directed render, so cloud shapes are illustrative of real cloud climatology, not a weather snapshot

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA elevation and imagery data
textures.note: The provider states its textures are tuned and contain fictional fill; this is a stylised city-lights layer, not the NASA Black Marble product.

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, MESSENGER MDIS Enhanced Color Global Mosaic 665 m
textures.credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington; USGS Astrogeology Science Center
textures.note: The source is an ENHANCED-colour (false-colour) product that exaggerates spectral differences. Only its luminance is used; the shader tints it to an approximate natural grey-brown (a visualisation choice).
textures.processing: converted to luminance, resampled to 2048x1024 and 512x256

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Io Galileo SSI/Voyager Global Color Merge Mosaic 1 km
textures.credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/USGS Astrogeology Science Center

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Europa Voyager/Galileo SSI Global Mosaic 500 m
textures.credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/USGS Astrogeology Science Center

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Ganymede Voyager/Galileo SSI Global Color Mosaic 1435 m
textures.credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/USGS Astrogeology Science Center

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Callisto Voyager/Galileo SSI Global Mosaic 1 km
textures.credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/USGS Astrogeology Science Center

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Enceladus Cassini ISS Global Mosaic 100 m (high-pass filtered)
textures.credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute/USGS Astrogeology Science Center
textures.note: High-pass-filtered (HPF) mosaic: albedo contrast, brightness is a processed product.

textures.source: USGS Astrogeology, Triton Voyager 2 Global Color Mosaic 600 m (with filled gaps)
textures.note: Voyager 2 imaged only part of Triton at useful resolution; the 'GlobalFill' product fills the unimaged hemisphere with lower-quality data, so those areas are not high-resolution observations.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA elevation and imagery data
textures.note: No manageable true-colour Mars mosaic could be obtained (the USGS Viking colour mosaic is 12.7 GB). The provider states its colours are tuned to Viking true-colour photos, slightly over-saturated, and that unmapped areas are filled with fictional terrain.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA data
textures.note: Venus's surface is permanently hidden by cloud. Visible-light images show a nearly featureless pale-yellow disc; this texture is a stylised cloud layer. No radar surface map is drawn.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA data
textures.note: Saturn has no fixed surface and no authoritative global cylindrical map was obtained. This is a stylised band pattern.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA data
textures.projection: radial strip (ring opacity as a function of radius)
textures.note: The radial extent the strip covers is not documented by the provider. Atlas calibrates it against known ring-feature radii (Cassini Division, A-ring outer edge) and records the result.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA data
textures.note: Voyager 2 saw Uranus as a nearly featureless pale cyan-blue disc; no global map exists. This is a stylised version.

textures.credit: Solar System Scope (INOVE), based on NASA data
textures.note: No global map of Neptune exists. This is a stylised version of its deep-blue appearance.
